payload.author: andrexibiza
payload.body:
Thanks for chasing the deleted-WAL generation rather than treating a pathname lock probe as proof of quiescence. The new real Linux subprocess regression is the right kind of witness: it keeps process A alive, unlinks the sidecar generation, and proves process B refuses before structural repair. Moving one holder detector behind both FTS maintenance and top-level repair is also directionally much better than a second copy.

I reviewed exact head `366df78fcdc253aceaa2ae3c6a8a2d4120de3a00`. Live `main` is `00bbfc690060d1323ddb2f065297c7425cb71c26`; the exact merge base is `baa344dee76993f0444c18fc59a69738ccb339d0`, so this head is 1 commit ahead / 3 behind current main. There were no prior review submissions or PR-thread comments on this head.

There are two correctness/landing blockers I would close before this is mergeable.

**P1 — the new repair admission promotes a holder predicate that already has two live, demonstrated identity defects.**

At `hermes_state.py` around the new `_foreign_state_db_holders()` / `_live_writer_holds_db()` boundary, the Linux detector still decides readable descriptors by canonicalized **path string**, and the uninspectable-fd fallback still decides “possible Hermes holder” from the current `_looks_like_hermes(cmdline)` heuristic. #97330 then makes either `"... (deleted)"` or `"uninspectable holder: ..."` an immediate top-level schema-repair refusal.

That matters because both weaknesses already have live corrective PRs with concrete witnesses:

- #96011 (`ciabata-git`) proves that a path string is not file identity across mount namespaces: a container can expose `/root/.hermes/state.db[-wal]` in host `/proc` while referring to a different `(st_dev, st_ino)`. Its patch pins descriptor identity to device+inode and retains path fallback only on the same filesystem for truly unlinked sidecars. The branch explicitly names this same `_foreign_state_db_holders()` function.
- #92419 (`fangliquanflq`) proves the unreadable-fd fallback can classify unrelated wrappers/log readers as Hermes merely because argv contains Hermes text; it replaces the flattened-string heuristic with argv-aware executable/module/script identity.

Before #97330 those defects can defer automatic FTS recovery. With this PR they also become reasons to refuse the operator’s top-level schema-repair path. In particular, a path-identical deleted sidecar from another mount namespace can satisfy `path.endswith(" (deleted)")`, and an unrelated uninspectable process can satisfy the `uninspectable holder:` arm, even though neither owns this database generation. That can strand repair of an already-damaged store — exactly the “other side” of making the safety gate stricter.

Please make the new shared detector authority-grade before widening its reach: either land #96011 and #92419 first and restack this PR onto their semantics, or absorb their two orthogonal fixes here with credit and tests. I’d specifically want the #96011 different-filesystem same-path witness and the #92419 unrelated-uninspectable-process negative witness run against the **same helper** used by `repair_state_db_schema()`, plus the deleted-WAL positive witness already added here. Do not allow three competing implementations of this predicate to land independently.

The merge-order/lineage graph here is important and should be explicit in the PR body. The holder guard originates in #90871 by `fangliquanflq`, was salvaged/landed with preserved authorship in #91839 by `kshitijk4poor`, and was further hardened by merged #93453 (`teknium1`, salvaging #93191) around durable deferral/re-scan semantics. #96011 and #92419 are complementary current corrections to the exact detector #97330 is now promoting; they are not duplicates of this top-level-repair fix. Please preserve that contributor lineage rather than only saying “reuse the existing scan.”

**P1 landing/ownership gate — do not grow/re-home another state authority inside the godfile.**

This head still adds the reusable hold

payload.author: andrexibiza
payload.body:
Fresh review of exact head `77ba9c8bc0b8e1903534735c0b2354ad49235f9f` against current `main` `ac6c8028e00d01ee2f299ba7fd03329c7f10382d`.

The prior attribution/composition blockers are genuinely fixed: the #92419 and #96011 commits retain their original authors, both contributor mappings are present, and the same-path/different-inode false-positive now has direct coverage. The real deleted-WAL subprocess witness also remains the right positive test. This head still has four blockers before the detector is authority-grade.

**P1 — path text still selects the candidate before inode identity is allowed to authorize it.**

In [`_foreign_state_db_holders()`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/77ba9c8bc0b8e1903534735c0b2354ad49235f9f/hermes_state.py#L3195-L3223), the code executes:

```python
if _canonical(target) not in watched:
    continue
fd_st = os.stat(fd_path)
```

That means `(st_dev, st_ino)` is consulted only after path equality has already admitted the descriptor. It fixes the false-positive direction demonstrated by #96011, but not the inverse: the same file identity reached through a hard link, bind mount, or mount-namespace alias is discarded before identity is checked. The current regression proves “same path, different inode is not ours”; it does not prove “different path, same inode is ours.”

This matters beyond the top-level repair probe because `_try_runtime_fts_rebuild()` consumes this helper directly as its foreign-holder admission decision. Identity needs to be checked independently of target spelling; path should remain only the narrowly justified fallback for an unreachable deleted generation. Add the inverse different-path/same-`(dev, ino)` witness, plus the stale-generation alias case if that fallback is intended to cover namespace aliases.

**P1 — `/proc` uncertainty flips between fail-open and fail-closed based only on where inspection failed.**

At [`hermes_state.py:3187-3205`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/77ba9c8bc0b8e1903534735c0b2354ad49235f9f/hermes_state.py#L3187-L3205):

- if the whole fd directory is unreadable, the process blocks only when argv matches the Hermes executable heuristic; an unreadable `sqlite3`, backup/diagnostic client, older entry point, arbitrary Python opener, or unreadable cmdline is silently treated as proof of quiescence even though it can hold the old generation;
- if the directory is readable but `readlink()` fails on one fd with any non-disappearance error, every process becomes a blocking `uninspectable descriptor` even though the code has not established that the fd points anywhere near `state.db`.

The same epistemic state — descriptor ownership is unknown — therefore permits unsafe surgery at one boundary and can permanently strand repair at the next. The policy cannot depend on failure depth or executable branding. Add paired end-to-end regressions for an unrecognized process with an unreadable fd table that really holds the generation, and an unrelated process with one unreadable non-state fd that must not block. Resolve both through one file/process-authority proof model.

**P1 — the macOS/BSD branch does not carry the stale-generation signal this fix requires, and its test fabricates the Linux signal.**

The non-Linux branch explicitly says there is no Linux-style `" (deleted)"` suffix and records only `psutil.open_files().path` ([`hermes_state.py:3236-3293`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/77ba9c8bc0b8e1903534735c0b2354ad49235f9f/hermes_state.py#L3236-L3293)). But `_live_writer_holds_db()` immediately blocks only unknown sentinels or a path ending in `" (deleted)"`; an ordinary path falls through to the replacement-path SQLite probe, which is exactly the probe that cannot see an unlinked old generation.

The Darwin regression does not exercise real Darwin semantics: it forces `sys.platform = "darwin"` while injecting `f"{db_path}-wal (deleted)"` into fake psutil data ([test lines 192-229](https://github.com/No

payload.author: Enough1122
payload.body:
> AI code review — automated review for reference, author can ignore or act on any point.

The negotiation ladder is well designed: try the OpenAI-style `video_url`, retry the llama.cpp `input_video` dialect only on a wire-format rejection, then fall back to bounded chronological JPEG frames — and every transition is authorized by the provider's actual response, never by guessing the endpoint or model name. The bounded ffmpeg subprocess calls (argv vectors, stdin disabled, per-call timeout, private temp dir with Windows-safe cleanup) and the evidence-note prompt that stops the model from inventing audio/continuity are both the right calls. The regression tests are genuinely thorough, including the real-ffmpeg integration test.

Points to consider:

1. **The frame-extraction implementation is duplicated and has already diverged.** `core.py` ships a full `_extract_video_frames`/`_probe_video_duration`/`_frame_timestamps`/`_jpeg_data_url` (~`core.py` L793-924), and `frames.py` ships near-identical copies of the same four functions (~`frames.py` L1581-1774). Then `tools/video_analysis/__init__.py` (L431-432) silently overwrites core's globals with frames' versions at import, so core's copy is dead code that only exists to be replaced. Worse, the two copies have already drifted: core's ffmpeg filter is `scale=w='min({max_side},iw)':h=-2` (constrains only width), while frames' is `scale={max_side}:{max_side}:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease:force_divisible_by=2` (the bounded variant the tests actually assert). Per the repo's extend-don't-duplicate rule, keep one implementation (frames.py is the better one — the bounded aspect handling) and have core import it, so the two can't silently disagree again.

2. **`_status_code` regex over-matches any 3-digit number** (`core.py` L1004-1012): `re.search(r"\b(?:http\s*)?(\d{3})\b", str(exc))` will read *any* three consecutive digits in an error message as an HTTP status. Provider messages routinely embed such numbers for unrelated reasons — e.g. `"stream ended after 429 bytes"`, `"model returned 404 tokens"`, `"attempt 429: retrying"` — and each would be misclassified as a fatal status, skipping the whole negotiation ladder (`_is_fatal_request_error` returns True → `_should_try_input_video`/`_should_try_frames` return False). Prefer `exc.status_code` / `response.status_code` only (already tried first), and if the string fallback must stay, anchor it to the leading position (`^(?:HTTP )?(\d{3})\b`) or restrict it to the first 20 chars.

3. **The 50 MB cap is enforced after reading the whole file into memory** (`core.py` L1323-1334): `_video_to_base64_data_url` calls `video_path.read_bytes()`, and only then is the encoded length checked against `_MAX_VIDEO_BASE64_BYTES`. `video_size_bytes` is already available at that point (`stat().st_size` at L1308) — a pre-check of `st_size` against the base64-inflated limit (~37 MB of raw video) would reject oversized inputs without buffering 50 MB first.

4. **`_resolve_video_call_settings` clamps the timeout to ≥ 180 s** (`core.py` L1212-1231): `timeout = max(float(configured_timeout), 180.0)`. That's defensible for a slow video round-trip, but it means a user who sets `auxiliary.video.timeout: 60` to fail fast is silently overridden. If the floor is intentional, a one-line comment saying so would prevent a confused config bug report; otherwise use the configured value directly.

5. **Registry dance depends on import order** (`core.py` L1545 + `__init__.py` L489 + `tools/vision_video_analysis.py` L1801): three registrations of `video_analyze` with `override=True`, relying on sorted module discovery to settle on the package owner. The discovery-bridge test pins the final state, which is good — just worth a comment near the `override=True` sites documenting that the ordering is load-bearing, so a future rename (e.g. `vision_video_analysis.py` sorting later than expected) doesn't silently regress which handler wins.

payload.author: andrexibiza
payload.body:
Reviewed exact head `80157e795ffc2f39dcc1a19eea7f561f01b2e29e` against the live multiplex-storage graph, the #66887 incident thread, merged #88734, the narrower historical #69042 objections, adjacent degraded-store work in #88804, and current main.

The core direction is right: moving session-row ownership from ambient `HERMES_HOME` to the profile already encoded in `agent:<profile>:…` closes the background-worker half that #88734 could not close. In particular, carrying `_db_for_key()` through expiry finalization, staleness checks, recovery, transcript mutation, reset/switch, and peer repair is the right shape. The field evidence showing opposite `end_reason` polarity in root vs profile stores is especially useful because it proves two independent writers rather than a single stale copy. The follow-up commit also correctly stopped memoizing a profile-home miss.

I found one P1 boundary that still recreates the exact wrong-store class during runtime enrollment:

### P1 — a named profile that is not live *yet* still falls through to the ambient/root DB

`_profile_home_for_key()` currently returns the same `None` for three semantically different states: multiplexing/default namespace, a named profile whose directory does not exist yet, and a profile-resolution exception. `_db_for_key()` then interprets every `None` as `return self._db`.

That matters because the new regression itself establishes that the enrollment bridge can legitimately expose a key before `profiles/<name>/` exists. On that first lookup, a key such as `agent:fitness:telegram:dm:1` therefore still resolves to the ambient root `state.db`; after enrollment creates the directory, the next lookup flips to `profiles/fitness/state.db`. That is two physical stores for one qualified session identity — precisely the split this PR is meant to eliminate. The same fail-open happens on a transient `profile_exists()` / `get_profile_dir()` error because the exception is also collapsed to `None`.

Please make ownership tri-state instead of using `None` for both “ambient is authoritative” and “named owner unavailable”:

- non-multiplex / legacy-default key → ambient DB, preserving current single-profile behavior;
- named profile + resolved home → that profile DB;
- named profile + missing/unresolvable home → no DB / defer or refuse the state mutation, never silently fall back to root.

The regression should exercise the real effect boundary, not just cache behavior: resolve a named key before its profile directory exists, attempt a representative write/read through `_db_for_key()`, and prove root `state.db` remains untouched; then create the profile and prove the same key lands only in the profile DB. Also cover the resolver-exception branch, because it currently has the same ambient fallback.

### Interlocks / landing edge

This is a continuation of #88734 rather than a duplicate: #88734 established per-active-scope handles and preserved the #88632 / `jackulau` lineage; this PR repairs the unscoped/background side by deriving ownership from the key. #69042 is historical architectural evidence for the still-unfinished routing-index half, not an alternate implementation. #88804 is complementary degraded-DB continuity work and should be reconciled at `load_transcript()` rather than treated as superseded.

The #66887 routing-index half remains real: `_entries` / `_loaded`, `_routing_scope()`, `gateway_routing`, and the `sessions.json` mirror are still one process-wide/frozen storage surface. I agree with keeping that out of this diff, but it must remain explicitly open and merge-ordered after this change; this PR should not be used as closure evidence for #66887 while that half can still disagree with the per-session owner.

Current topology also needs a fresh landing object. The reviewed head is **2 ahead / 133 behind** live `main@e387cbc0aa0fc89560bc14438762c7722663db05`. I checked the main-side history since the merge base and there are no newer commits touching `gateway/sessio

Thanks — both notes are fair. The second one is a real bug, so I've pushed a fix (`80157e7`).

**Memo not invalidated.** It's sharper than deletion, actually: the *miss* was cached, so a profile that appears **after** the gateway starts stays pinned to the ambient store for the life of the process — precisely the failure this helper exists to prevent. That isn't hypothetical: an enrollment bridge can provision `profiles/<name>/` at runtime, so a key is legitimately seen before its directory exists. `_profile_home_for_key` now memoizes only hits; a miss costs one `profile_exists()` stat and recurs only for profiles that genuinely don't exist, so the hot path for real profiles is still a dict hit. `test_profile_home_is_not_memoized_before_the_profile_exists` covers it — it fails without the change.

payload.author: fangliquanflq
payload.title: fix(agent): stop incomplete runs from reporting success

payload.author: Enough1122
payload.body:
> AI code review — automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

**Overall:** Important contract fix at two outer boundaries that stops empty/partial incomplete turns from being recorded as `run.completed`. Classifies existing `completed/failed/partial` signals without touching the 26 inner early-return sites.

**What it does**
- `run_agent.py:8980` at outer `run_conversation` finally computes `terminal_incomplete = failed is True or completed is False or partial is True`; if incomplete and `turn_exit_reason` absent, stamps `terminal["turn_exit_reason"]="early_return"` and `logger.warning("Turn ended: reason=early_return completed=…")` (redacted error ≤500), and maps `relay_outcome` to `failed` (vs cancelled/success) — ensures `finish_logical_calls(outcome=failed)` and metrics reflect failure even when `finalize_turn` was bypassed.
- `gateway/platforms/api_server.py:7880` in `_run_sync` widens `elif failed:` to `(failed is True or completed is False or partial is True)`, propagates `final_response` as `output`, `completed`/`partial` into both `run.failed` event and `run status=failed` (mirroring `/v1/chat/completions` already does).
- Tests `tests/gateway/test_api_server_runs.py:126` param `("",False)` and `("partial answer",True)` assert `status==failed`, `completed is False`, etc.; `tests/run_agent/test_run_agent.py:3267` asserts `finish_logical_calls(outcome==failed)` and `Turn ended:` warning.

**Non-blocking notes**
- Strict `is True` / `is False` checks avoid truthy coercion — e.g. `completed=None` not treated as incomplete (only explicit `False`) — matches intended contract; ensure older callers never emit `"false"` string.
- Stamping `turn_exit_reason` only when missing avoids overwriting genuine reason from inner path; good scoping.
- Login to `logger.warning` includes `response_len` and `api_calls` — helpful for empty-output diagnosis.

*Non-blocking — please use your judgment.*

payload.author: woprrr
payload.title: feat(dashboard): withhold deployment detail from anonymous /api/status callers

payload.author: Enough1122
payload.body:
> AI code review — automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

**Overall:** Sound security hardening for self-hosted dashboard on the internet. Keeps default `full` to preserve Hermes Cloud Portal behavior (unauthenticated profile list), while `minimal` withholds deployment detail (`profiles`/`gateway_mode`/`memory`/`disk`) from anonymous callers on gated bind and restores it for valid sessions (cookie or `Bearer`).

**What it does**
- `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:1637` and `cli-config.yaml.example:1888` add `dashboard.public_status_detail` (`full` vs `minimal`, env `HERMES_DASHBOARD_PUBLIC_STATUS_DETAIL`, env wins, case-insensitive `minimal` check, fail-open to `full` on unreadable config with warning).
- `hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/middleware.py:320` adds `_attach_public_path_session(request)` — best-effort attach of `request.state.session` for public paths (`_path_is_public` branch) via `Bearer` then `Provider.verify_session`, never failing request (stale cookie/bearer/unreachable IDP → anonymous).
- `hermes_cli/web_server.py:3740` adds `_public_status_detail()` and makes `get_status(request, profile)` withhold: `withhold = auth_required and detail==minimal and session is None and not token_authenticated`; when withheld skips `collect_memory_status`/`collect_disk_status` (side benefit: no `statvfs`/heartbeat reads) and omits `status["profiles"]`/`status["gateway_mode"]`; liveness (`version`, `gateway_state`, `install_id`, session counts, auth-gate shape) stays public.
- Docs `website/docs/user-guide/features/web-dashboard.md:398` and tests `tests/hermes_cli/test_dashboard_auth_status_endpoint.py:95` cover default full, minimal anonymous withhold, signed-in keep, broken cookie probe still 200, bearer keeps, loopback no-op, env override wins.

**Non-blocking notes**
- `fail open` on unreadable config is correct for liveness (probe must not 500) but silently drops hardening — logged as warning; ensure log is visible to operator reviewing config.
- `request` param default `None` for in-process callers — treated as anonymous (good seam); ensure no direct internal caller expects full detail and now loses it when unauthenticated.
- `token_authenticated` flag check alongside `session` handles JS SDK case where bearer verified but session shape differs — complete.

*Non-blocking — please use your judgment.*

payload.author: woprrr
payload.body:
Thanks for the review. Verified each note against the branch; one was actionable and is now fixed.

**Fail-open warning visibility.** You were right to look at it, and it was worse than "is it visible": the warning sat on a per-request path. `/api/status` is polled on a timer by portals, uptime monitors and the desktop, so a single unreadable config would emit one warning per probe and bury the line the operator needs. Now warned once per process, following the same one-shot discipline as the malformed-`public_url` warnings in `dashboard_auth/prefix.py`. A test asserts three probes produce exactly one warning, and it fails without the guard. Pushed.

**In-process callers losing detail.** Checked: the only direct caller of `web_server.get_status` outside the ASGI route is `tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server.py`, which asserts the config load stays off the event loop and does not read `profiles` / `memory` / `disk`. Every other consumer arrives over HTTP and therefore carries a `Request`. No production caller loses anything.

**`token_authenticated`.** Small correction: that flag is set only for routes registered via `register_token_route` (today the drain endpoint), and `/api/status` is not one of them, so it never fires there. The bearer case is handled by `_attach_public_path_session`, which verifies the `Authorization: Bearer` token through the same provider stack before falling back to the cookie. The flag stays in the condition as defence in depth if `/api/status` ever becomes token-authable, and `test_status_keeps_operator_detail_for_bearer_caller` covers the real path.

One nit for future automated passes: the line anchors in the summary have drifted. The new key is `config_defaults.py:1648`, the helper is `middleware.py:323`, `_public_status_detail` is `web_server.py:3743`, and the example config entry is `cli-config.yaml.example:1901`.
